bugs.text: drawTitle uses SPR.boss and SPR.zako, which do not exist (the sprites are boss1/zako1). drawSprite throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading rows)' on every title frame: this is the cause of all 601 console errors in result.json.

The title exception skips ctx.restore(), so each frame's ctx.save();ctx.scale(scale,scale) compounds. Within a few frames the transform is scale^N and everything is drawn off-canvas, and the fillRect at 464 blacks out the canvas under that transform. The screen stays black even after Enter (every screenshot is black; starts=false, moves=false).
fire() is never called and keys.fire is never read: the player can never shoot, so no enemy can ever be destroyed and no stage can be cleared.

Inside updateShots, `let hit=false` shadows the hit() collision function, so `hit(s.x-2,...)` would throw 'hit is not a function' every frame a shot exists, aborting update() (and skipping render) until the shot leaves the screen. Even if fire() were wired, shots could never hit anything.

launchGroup() is never called and G.entryTimer never counts down. Every enemy stays in state 'waiting' for the whole stage: no entry flight (they sit in their slots via line 306), never reach 'formation', so no dives (309), no enemy fire (313), no breathing (269), and they are immune to shots (285).
shootPlayer calls Sound.eshot(), which is not defined on the Sound object (104-137): TypeError before the bullet is pushed. Enemies could never fire even if they reached a firing state.

No 'returning' path is ever assigned (makeReturnPath unused); a diver past t=1 keeps following the extrapolated quadratic off the bottom for ever, never re-enters and can never be killed, so a stage with any diver could never be cleared.
No code ever sets an enemy's state to 'beam'. The tractor beam, capture, captured fighter, rescue, dual fighter and captive fire (E1-E6) can never trigger.

updateStageEnd increments stageTextT once per fixed step while render decrements it once per frame; at 60 Hz (or higher) it never reaches the 150/230 threshold, so the 'stageend' state never advances: soft-lock after a stage clear.

In a challenging stage buildFormation() still creates 40 enemies in state 'entering' with path=null and setupEntryGroups is skipped; updateEnemies line 301 then throws on e.path.dur every step, freezing the stage.
There is no enemy-body vs player collision at all (pHitTest is only used for bullets); ramming an enemy does nothing, and the rammed enemy is not destroyed.
The per-frame clear fillRect(0,0,GW,GH) runs before ctx.scale, so only a 224x288 device-pixel corner is cleared; at scale 2 or more the rest of the canvas keeps old frames (smeared trails).
updateTitle sets G.high=G.score every 40 frames, wiping the high score loaded from localStorage; saveHigh then stores the last game's score, not the record.
Single fighter is limited to 1 shot on screen (G.dual?2:1), not 2 as in the arcade.
goei2 is identical to goei1 and boss2/bossHit2 identical to boss1/bossHit1: no wing-flap animation for Goei or Boss Galaga.
The first hit on a Boss Galaga awards 50 points; the arcade awards nothing until it is destroyed.
G.respawnDelay is set to 85 on a life loss but never decremented, so dives and enemy fire are blocked permanently after the first death.
'READY' is only shown at stage start (readyT set once in startStage), not when the player respawns.
drawStageEnd (NUMBER OF HITS, BONUS, PERFECT!) is never called from render.
A captive is freed whenever its boss dies, including when the boss is shot in formation (spec: captive is destroyed then).

Escorts keep their old t (not reset) so they start their dive path two-thirds of the way along; the 'dying' flag set when the leader dies is never processed, leaving escorts snapped to their slot while still in 'dive' state.
Challenging-stage enemies loop around an ellipse for ever (no exit), and a wave only ends when all 8 are destroyed.
The title score table draws the Zako sprite for the Goei row (only 'boss' is special-cased).
The starfield does not scroll on the title screen (updateStars only runs while playing).
render() mutates game state (stageTextT, readyT), tying those timers to the frame rate instead of the fixed step.

summary: The file is tidy on the surface: clearly sectioned constants, data sprites, a synthesized Sound object, a fixed-step rAF loop, and a plausible model of Galaga's rules (two-hit bosses, escort-based scoring, capture/rescue/dual-fighter states, challenging waves, badge denominations). Almost none of it is connected. Two typos (SPR.boss/SPR.zako, Sound.eshot) and a variable shadowing the hit() function make the title screen throw every frame, and the unbalanced ctx.save() turns the whole game permanently black, which is exactly what the play-test shows. Behind that, fire() is never called, launchGroup() is never called so enemies never enter the formation state, no enemy ever enters the 'beam' state, divers never return, the stage-end timer can never elapse at 60 Hz, and the challenging stage dereferences a null path. Scores above zero were given only where an item's own code is complete and wired (HUD, controls, lives/extra-ship rule, point table, layout, badges, audio gating); every signature mechanic of Galaga (entry flights, breathing formation, dives, tractor beam, dual fighter, challenging stages) is dead code. As delivered it is a black screen, not a game.
